title: Applications of the Lorentz positive cone in nonconvex quadratic optimization
contribution: Uses Hildebrand's polynomial LMI for the Lorentz positive cone and its dual (the Lorentz separable cone) to give an exact SEP formulation and a polynomial-time bisection-plus-TRS-oracle algorithm for bilinear optimization over two ellipsoids, and to strengthen the Shor SDP for quadratic problems over two ellipsoids, TTRS and a noxious location problem, with a certified n = 2 counterexample showing SEP+Shor is not exact for TTRS.
problem_entry: Entered from a tool: Hildebrand's exact (polynomial-size) LMI for LOP(n, m), a long-open question, asking which QP class it solves exactly and what it adds to Shor for harder classes; the LMI's size beyond about n, m = 30 motivates a separation oracle (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: The off-diagonal block Z = [1 x'; y V] of the Shor matrix lies in SEP(n+1, m+1), which with Z00 = 1 is exactly the hull of (1; y)(1; x)' over unit balls (Lemma 3, p. 5); solved as Full SEP, Lazy SEP (equalities added as needed) or by bisection on the one dual variable with a TRS-based LOP membership oracle (pp. 4-7).
assumptions: min(n, m) >= 2; full-dimensional ellipsoids reduced WLOG to unit balls; TTRS with A nonsingular and Q stated indefinite (p. 13) though the counterexample uses negative definite Q (p. 16); polynomial time rests on poly-time TRS [8] and Hildebrand's LMI cited, not reproved (pp. 2-6, 13).
proof_devices: Proposition 2: SEP LMI derived by conic duality/minimax from Hildebrand's LOP LMI (Proposition 1) (pp. 3-4)
TRS-based separation oracle with explicit separating matrix yx' (eq. (4), p. 4)
Lemma 3 normalization of Lorentz rank-one atoms into a convex combination (p. 5)
Lemma 4 nuclear-norm bound via weighted deviation decomposition and Cauchy-Schwarz; Corollary 5 boundary via Frobenius perturbation (pp. 5-6)
Lemma 6: Pataki rank bound, rank-one Schur complement, so the rank-2 Shor optimum is not interior to SEP (p. 10); Lemma 8 extends it to TTRS through the linear map G (p. 14)
Lemma 7: SEP implies KRON by atom-by-atom check; explicit explanation why it fails for TTRS (pp. 11, 15)
Bisection bracket from norm inequalities and primal recovery from the oracle's violating pair (p. 7)
Appendix: Schur-complement block elimination turning a violated KRON LMI into a linear cut (pp. 21-22)
TTRS non-exactness counterexample at n = 2 with rational data, value certified by enumerating stationary points and arc intersections and confirmed by Gurobi to nine digits (p. 16)
Exact noxious-location optimum by O(m^3) Voronoi-candidate enumeration (p. 18)
experiments: Mac mini M4, MOSEK 11.2.2, Gurobi 13.0.2, Python 3.14.6, solver defaults, code at github.com/sburer/lorentz-positive (p. 8); four families: 120 bilinear instances filtered by Shor gap > 0.01 (p. 8), 90 max-distance instances after a rank-one screen scanning up to 16970 seeds (pp. 11-13), the 212 unsolved TTRS instances of the 2013 paper plus 30 new Shor-not-tight ones (pp. 15-16), noxious location on regular m-gons and random points (pp. 18-20); baselines Shor, RLT, KRON, Lazy KRON, beta relaxation, Gurobi with adaptive time limit; tight = gap (19) <= 1e-5 against a method-specific recovered feasible point (p. 12); losses printed (Lazy SEP slower on small bilinear and m-gon instances, pp. 9, 19).
positioning: Builds on Hildebrand [10, 11] and credits Nemirovski for the oracle idea while giving an independent oracle (pp. 2, 4); places SEP in the authors' own TTRS lineage (SOC-RLT 2013, KRON 2017, beta 2025), concedes all 212 test problems were already solved by [3] and [4] (p. 16), and reports an instance where Burer's own beta relaxation fails to be exact (p. 17).
writing: Three-sentence abstract, roadmap at end of introduction (p. 2), graded claim language ('very likely' pp. 10, 14; 'To our knowledge' p. 17; 'we have determined' p. 16), summary paragraph after each experiment (pp. 9, 13), two-sentence conclusion (p. 20), AI use for code and light editing disclosed (p. 20).
limits_future: Explicit LMI impractical beyond about 30 (p. 2); SEP+Shor not exact for TTRS (n = 2 counterexample, 15.74% gap, p. 16); SEP does not close noxious-location gaps in general and its relative improvement over Shor shrinks with m (p. 19); SEP-over-KRON dominance not extended to TTRS (p. 15); future work is one generic line on further applications (p. 20).

method_links.note: Bilinear problem over two ellipsoids written exactly as a linear problem over SEP(n+1, m+1) with Z00 = 1; hardness sits in one cone attacked by LMI, lazy equalities and a dual oracle; cheaper routes built because the explicit LMI is too large (Method 1 stop rule).

SEP tested against the beta relaxation that already contains Shor, RLT, SOC-RLT and Kronecker constraints; noxious-location ladder Shor >= RLT >= KRON >= Full SEP >= true on every instance; claim bounded by an n = 2 counterexample.

Non-exactness for TTRS shown by a counterexample with rational data certified two ways (enumeration plus Gurobi to nine digits); counterexample also published against the author's own 2025 beta relaxation; tight = 1e-5 gap to a recovered feasible point.
No exact rational certificate printed for the counterexample, only decimal values.

Shor-gap > 0.01 filter for bilinear instances, rank-one screen with up to 16970 seeds for max-distance, the 2013 unsolved 212-instance TTRS set reused and a harder Shor-not-tight rung n = 20, 25, 30 added.
Seed-scan counts not reported for the bilinear family or the 30 new TTRS instances; disclosure applied to one family only.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Import an exact cone description from linear algebra and pair it with a cheap oracle
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Hildebrand's LOP/SEP LMI from Linear and Multilinear Algebra used as given, then a TRS separation oracle, lazy subspace equalities and bisection make it computable at sizes where the LMI is not.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Rank-2 boundary argument as the motivation for a new constraint
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Pataki rank bound plus a nuclear-norm equality shows the rank-2 Shor optimum cannot be interior to SEP, so adding SEP is 'very likely' to cut it off; used for both the two-ellipsoid QP and TTRS.

transferable: Reduce membership in a cone of maps L^m -> L^n to a trust-region subproblem and read the separating rank-one matrix yx' off its minimizer (p. 4).
Bisect on a one-dimensional dual with a membership oracle; take the initial bracket from norm bounds and recover an eps-optimal primal point from the oracle's non-membership certificate (p. 7).
Enforce a large linear-subspace constraint lazily: add at most 50 most-violated equalities per round to a relative tolerance 1e-7 scaled by ||S||_F (pp. 7-8).
Prove that a new cone constraint dominates an old one atom by atom, and when a coupling constraint is not inherited by the atoms, state which proof step fails (pp. 11, 15).
Measure each relaxation's gap against a feasible point recovered from its own solution, never another method's incumbent (p. 12).
Before counting an instance as having a gap, screen out spuriously high-rank SDP optima by re-solving with the objective fixed and a random linear objective (p. 12).
Give the global solver an instance-adaptive limit max{5, 3 t_max} tied to the slowest conic method and report how many it certifies (pp. 8, 12).
For 2-D test problems, compute exact optima by finite candidate enumeration (Voronoi vertices, bisector-edge intersections, hull vertices) (p. 18).

quotes.text: Although the addition of the SEP constraint to the Shor relaxation solves all of the problems considered above, we have determined that it is not sufficient to give an exact representation for TTRS.
This gives a method-specific feasible upper bound; no Gurobi incumbent or point recovered by another method is used to calculate the gap.
